props.caption: Keep the locks. Build the two named paths. Reject pane injection.

props.content:
A target admits only when authenticated, idle, unblocked, and its editor is empty. Waiting requests recheck after native editor input, idle, UI-unblock, or cooperating unblock. They never overwrite a draft.

There is one external slot, not a queue. A receipt means durable acceptance, not successful work. `message_start` is processing. `agent_settled` releases the slot. A turn may settle without an addressed reply.

props.summary: Why Herdr is the wrong bus

props.content:
Herdr owns workspaces, tabs, and panes. It can start a named agent in a shell pane and prompt that occupant. That is driving another process, not speaking as Shanon inside it.

Pane IDs change when a pane moves. Closed IDs are not reused. A session file can be forked, copied, or compacted. None of those are stable inboxes. Named agent address is.

Call-home still uses named correspondence: Shanon sends to the one Main Pi conversation that owns him. Same idle and empty-editor rules. Same one-slot default.

It is not "post into whatever tab I was looking at." If that home conversation is busy or the editor has a draft, the send waits or fails visibly.
